record.paper_title: Constructing groups of 'small' order: Recent results and open problems
record.context_brief: Counting groups of a given order
record.original_question: Let L_n denote a set containing one representative of each isomorphism type of finite group of order n, so |L_n| is the number of isomorphism types of groups of order n. Is there a closed formula for |L_n|, or a general method that determines |L_n| for arbitrary n without explicitly listing all groups?

artifact.self_contained_problem: For a positive integer $n$, let $L_n$ denote a complete set of representatives, one from each isomorphism class, of the finite groups of order $n$, and let $g(n) = |L_n|$ denote the number of isomorphism classes of finite groups of order $n$. Determine whether there exists a closed-form expression for $g(n)$ as a function of $n$, or more generally a procedure that computes $g(n)$ for arbitrary $n$ without enumerating, up to isomorphism, all groups of order $n$.
artifact.status_search_result: No closed formula or general method is known for computing the number of isomorphism types of groups of order $n$. Partial results exist: a clean formula for abelian groups via prime-power factorizations, and Higman–Sims asymptotics for prime-power orders. Computationally, $g(n)$ is known for $n \le 2047$, with $n = 2048 = 2^{11}$ the smallest open case. The general enumeration problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Number of groups of order n - OEIS Wiki
status_evidence.snippet: There is no known formula which gives the number of groups of order n for an arbitrary positive integer n.
status_evidence.claim: No general closed formula is known.

status_evidence.title: Number of groups of given order - Groupprops
status_evidence.snippet: The number of groups of order n is known for small n, with the smallest unknown order being 2048.
status_evidence.claim: Computation is feasible for small n, but no general formula exists.
